set.typical_award_size: Section 20.234.010 (Ord. No. 4538, September 10, 2024) establishes an Affordable Housing Trust Fund to receive all funds collected under Chapter 20.234 (equity-sharing payments on density bonus for-sale units) and monies from other sources, administered by a Board-designated nonprofit and spent per the Housing Element to construct, rehabilitate or subsidize housing for extremely low through moderate income households, with an annual Board accounting. No deposits, designated administrator or awards were found in Board records.
set.layering_notes: Mendocino County has no housing department: the Executive Office Grants Division administers state CDBG and HOME program income, Social Services is the administrative entity for the Mendocino County Homeless Services Continuum of Care (CA-509) and HHAP, Behavioral Health and Recovery Services holds BHSA, NPLH and bridge housing, Planning and Building Services handles density bonus and the Housing Element, and the Community Development Commission of Mendocino County (CDC, the housing authority) supplies vouchers and owns housing. The County repealed its inclusionary ordinance on September 10, 2024, has no housing trust fund money, no NOFA and no impact fee waiver; County capital help has come from state pass-through grants (CDBG-DR, Homekey) and small HOME program income balances. Ukiah and Fort Bragg run their own programs (Pass 3). mendocinocounty.gov, the Legistar web API client 'mendocino', mendocino.granicusideas.com and cdchousing.org all open normally. Confirmation needed on whether any balance exists; the 2024 code created the vehicle without a revenue stream, so treat it as a future possibility only. Source is Ordinance No. 4538 (Inland Zoning Code Update, adopted September 10, 2024, Legistar item 24-0848), Section 20.234.010; zoneomics carries the same text. A Legistar title search found no item designating an administrator or depositing funds.
set.audit_note: funding_type kept as other: the fund has no revenue stream, no balance and no designated administrator, so nothing is deployable; reclassify to loan or grant if the Board capitalizes it and sets terms. Source moved from the zoneomics mirror to the official ordinance on Legistar.

reason: Official Ordinance 4538 text confirms the fund terms; tags broadened to match the ordinance and funding_type kept other because nothing is deployable.

set.next_deadline: No open RFP as of November 8, 2026 (CDC Project Bids and Awards: none at this time); a LIHTC or HOME project competitively selected within the prior three years can request PBVs without a new competition.
set.cycle_notes: No fixed cycle. CDC selects PBV projects by competitive RFP when issued, or without a new competition for projects selected under LIHTC, HOME or similar competitions within three years (Administrative Plan Chapter XXI, adopted May 15, 2025).
set.prevailing_wage_basis: Federal Davis-Bacon wages apply when a PBV Agreement to enter into HAP Contract covers development (new construction or rehabilitation) of nine or more contract units, per 24 CFR 983.154(b) as stated in CDC Administrative Plan Chapter XXI, Labor Standards (https://cdchousing.org/plan/21.%20Project%20Based%20Vouchers.pdf). PBVs on existing housing do not trigger it.

reason: Programs page and Chapter XXI confirm the voucher facts, no open RFP, and Davis-Bacon for nine or more newly constructed or rehabilitated PBV units.

set.affordability_requirement: Units restricted to lower income households by a recorded regulatory agreement or deed restriction, with tax savings used to maintain affordability or reduce rents; property must have state or federal LIHTC or government financing, or (nonprofit-owned, BOE-267-L) 90% or more qualified low-income tenants (BOE Publication 149). Lower income means up to 80% AMI under state law; exemption applies to qualifying units.
set.next_deadline: File BOE-267 (first filing) or BOE-267-A (annual) with the BOE-267-L or BOE-267-L1 supplemental affidavit with the Assessor by 5:00 p.m. February 16, 2027 for the 2027-28 roll (the February 15 deadline falls on Presidents Day, so it moves to the next business day per BOE Publication 149).
set.cycle_notes: Annual claim filing, not a NOFA: claims are due each year on or before February 15 for full exemption (next business day if a weekend or holiday); late claims may receive partial exemption. The managing general partner needs a BOE Organizational Clearance Certificate and, for limited partnerships, a Supplemental Clearance Certificate.
